title: What to watch at the open
text: Today is Veterans Day. The stock market is open at the normal time, but the bond market is closed, so trading may be a bit quieter than usual. Yesterday SPY fell 0.4% and QQQ fell 0.7% after a hot inflation report. At the open, watch NVIDIA, which is sitting just above its lowest price of the past year, and watch whether yesterday's winners, like Broadcom, Rocket Lab and Lockheed Martin, keep going or give some of it back.

title: NVIDIA sits near its 52 week low
text: NVIDIA closed near $168.90, down 5.5% on Tuesday. That is only about 3% above its 52 week low of $164.27 and about 31% below its high. Questions about the CEO are still in the news, and the company reports its quarterly results on November 17. Its risk score is 5.7 out of 10, which is medium.

title: Broadcom has its best two days in a while
text: Broadcom jumped about 8.8% on Monday and another 3.9% on Tuesday, to about $332. Reports say it set December 9 as the date for its next results. Even after this jump, it is still about 33% below its 52 week high. Big moves up can reverse just as fast, so this is one to watch, not to chase.

title: Eli Lilly is close to its high
text: Eli Lilly rose 1.4% to about $1,432. That puts it about 1% below its 52 week high of $1,453. Its risk score is 3.1 out of 10, one of the lowest on our list. When a stock sits near its high, it shows investors feel good about it, but it also means a lot of good news may already be in the price.

title: Lesson 46: What is a rate hike?
text: The Federal Reserve sets a key interest rate. That rate affects how much it costs to borrow money for things like houses, cars and business loans. A rate hike means the Fed raises that rate. The Fed usually does this to slow down rising prices, called inflation. When borrowing costs more, people and companies tend to spend less, and prices cool off. Stocks often fall when a hike looks more likely, because companies may earn less and safe savings accounts and bonds start to pay more. That is why yesterday's hot inflation report pushed stocks down.
